question: What controls the opening and closing of stomata?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Guard cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The opening and closing of **stomata** is primarily controlled by the **Guard cells**. These are specialized cells located in the **epidermis** of leaves and stems.
 
• Each stomatal pore is surrounded by a pair of **kidney-shaped** guard cells (in dicots) or **dumb-bell shaped** guard cells (in grasses/monocots).
 
• The mechanism of opening and closing depends on the **turgidity** of these cells. When water flows into the guard cells, they swell and become **turgid**, which pulls the stomatal pore open.
 
• Conversely, when the guard cells lose water, they shrink and become **flaccid**, causing the stomatal pore to close. This process helps the plant regulate **gas exchange** and **transpiration**.
